steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Spectators: People who watch sporting events, either at the venue in person or through media coverage. Spectators are a vital part of the sporting experience, providing atmosphere, revenue and motivation for performers. | Hooliganism: Disorderly, aggressive and violent behaviour by spectators at sporting events, most commonly associated with football. Hooliganism involves organised groups of fans who engage in fighting, vandalism and intimidation, often planning confrontations in advance. | PE Exam Tips — Spectator Behaviour and Hooliganism: 1. For Spectator Behaviour and Hooliganism questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain three positive effects of spectators on sport. | Describe three causes of hooliganism and explain how each contributes to spectator disorder. | Explain how banning orders work and evaluate their effectiveness in reducing hooliganism.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Spectators, Hooliganism, and one past-paper question.
